headline: CEAT warns of additional price hikes as raw material costs climb
hook: CEAT signals further tyre price hikes ahead
summary: CEAT CFO Kumar Subbiah stated the company has already increased tyre prices by 16% to 17% in the first half of FY27. Rising crude oil and raw material costs, exacerbated by Middle East tensions, are driving these expenses. The company anticipates a further 4% to 5% increase in input costs during Q3. CEAT estimates an additional 6% to 7% price hike is required to fully offset current margin pressures.
why_it_matters: Higher vehicle maintenance costs for consumers and potential margin compression for CEAT.
winners_losers: Raw material suppliers gain / Vehicle owners hurt

headline: CEAT Q2 net profit plunges 39.8% to Rs 112 crore on high raw material costs
hook: Margins shrink despite strong revenue growth
summary: CEAT reported a mixed Q2 FY27 performance as revenue rose 26.2% year-on-year to Rs 4,762 crore while net profit dropped 39.8% to Rs 112 crore. EBITDA declined 9.1% to Rs 457 crore, and margins contracted from 13.3% to 9.6% due to elevated commodity inflation and the West Asia crisis. CFO Kumar Subbiah outlined plans for Rs 490 crore in quarterly capex, capacity expansion, and potential price hikes to counter rising costs. Indian retail investors tracking auto ancillaries must watch how sustained raw material pressures impact tyre makers' profitability.
whats_next: Q3 FY27 results and margin recovery progress
why_it_matters: Rising commodity costs squeeze tyre maker profitability despite higher sales.
winners_losers: Raw material suppliers gain / CEAT hurt

headline: CEAT expects margin pressure to continue into Q3 due to high input costs
hook: Unprecedented price hikes fail to offset costs
summary: CEAT CFO Kumar Subbiah stated that margin pressure will likely persist through the third quarter of FY27. To combat rising input costs, the company implemented an unprecedented 16 to 17 percent price hike across several product categories during the first half of the fiscal year. Premium passenger tyres remain a key focus area for the tyre maker as it navigates these cost headwinds. Indian retail investors tracking auto ancillary stocks should note how raw material inflation impacts profitability despite aggressive pricing actions.
why_it_matters: Persisting margin pressures could weigh on CEAT's near-term profitability.
winners_losers: Raw material suppliers gain / tyre manufacturers hurt
